notes_or_caveats: One Stop Centres operate under the Ministry of Women and Child Development to provide integrated support to women affected by violence. Because these records contain highly sensitive, private psychological narratives and survivor vulnerabilities, police must handle the documents with extreme confidentiality. The data obtained from an OSC is heavily leveraged as corroborative evidence to establish historical patterns of cruelty or domestic abuse under the BNS.

entity_name: Child Welfare Committee (CWC) / Juvenile Justice Board (JJB)
what_they_can_provide: Social Investigation Reports (SIR) compiled by Probation Officers or Child Welfare Officers
Age determination enquiry orders, ossification test records, and matriculation certificate verifications accepted by the board
Orders for temporary placement, institutional care, or restoration of a Child in Need of Care and Protection (CNCP)
Bail, rehabilitation, or institutional custody orders for a Child in Conflict with the Law (CCL)
Individual Care Plans (ICP) and psychological counseling tracking records
legal_basis_typically_cited: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (Sections 4, 7, 27, 29, 94 regarding powers, procedures, and age determination)
BNSS Section 94 (formerly CrPC Section 91) - subject to absolute statutory confidentiality overrides under the JJ Act
request_format_expected: Formal administrative application or compliance report submitted by the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) or Child Welfare Police Officer (CWPO) directly before the Principal Magistrate of the Juvenile Justice Board (for CCL cases) or the Chairperson of the Child Welfare Committee (for CNCP cases). Requisitions must be filed using the statutory forms prescribed under the Juvenile Justice Model Rules.
typical_response_time: 24 hours for emergency production and safety placement orders; 3 to 7 working days for processing certified orders or copies of Social Investigation Reports (approximate)
escalation_path_if_no_response: Move an application before the Principal Magistrate of the JJB or approach the Children's Court / Court of Sessions; report administrative structural delays to the District Child Protection Unit (DCPU) or State Child Protection Society.
notes_or_caveats: The Juvenile Justice framework is an independent, non-adversarial statutory system that overrides regular police powers. Police officers cannot treat the JJB or CWC as subordinate record houses. Under Section 99 of the JJ Act, all records concerning a juvenile are strictly confidential and cannot be published or utilized in standard adult criminal trial procedures except as authorized by the Act. Crucially, any police interaction regarding these records must happen through the designated Child Welfare Police Officer (CWPO) wearing civilian clothes.

entity_name: Prisons Department (State Jail Administration)
what_they_can_provide: Inmate admission profiles, finger/palm print biometrics, and baseline identification photographs
Jail entry/exit visitor logs (Mulaqat registers detailing visitor names, addresses, IDs, and relationships)
Official prisoner health examination charts and medical officer reports
Internal prison CCTV footage from barracks, corridors, gates, and visitor meeting screens
Prisoner currency accounts (Jail canteen spending accounts and deposit tracking logs)
Records of disciplinary infractions, inside-jail offenses, parole/furlough histories, and release orders
legal_basis_typically_cited: BNSS Section 94 (formerly CrPC Section 91) for production of jail registers and logs
Prisons Act, 1894 (provisions governing jail discipline and internal management)
Prison Manuals of the respective state; Court warrants for production of prisoners (e.g., Section 293 BNSS / formerly 267 CrPC)
request_format_expected: Written notice under Section 94 BNSS signed by an officer not below the rank of SHO/IO, or a specific production warrant issued by a competent court, addressed directly to the Superintendent of the Central/District Jail where the inmate is or was lodged.
typical_response_time: 24 to 72 hours for routine visitor logs and admission documents; immediate for active production warrants or emergency safety queries (approximate)
escalation_path_if_no_response: Escalate to the Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Prisons or Director General (DG) of Prisons / Inspector General of Correctional Services of the respective state; notify the jurisdictional trial court.
notes_or_caveats: Prison administration is strictly a state subject, meaning prison manuals and digitization depth vary by region. Modern facilities use automated inmate tracking applications (like e-Prisons portal under the Inter-operable Criminal Justice System - ICJS), allowing synchronized cross-matching of inmate data across states. To question a currently jailed inmate or obtain active biometrics, a police investigator must secure a formal interrogation or production order from the jurisdictional magistrate rather than using a standard Section 94 notice alone.
